svg.title: Availability as the product of exit count, state synchronisation and detection speed, with four combinations and their user experience
svg.desc: Three factor cards multiply into availability: exit count with truly separated links, devices and pools, where a shared layer still counts as one; whether state can be synchronised, covering NAT bindings, firewall sessions and VPN security associations, with values of synchronised, rebuilt or lost; and detection speed through BFD, IP SLA, BGP or a human, with values from sub-second to minutes. A four-row table multiplies the combination into user experience: two exits with lost state and minute-level detection gives routing switched, every session broken and a forty-minute complaint; two exits with synchronised state but minute-level detection keeps sessions alive while traffic still follows the broken path for 180 seconds; two exits with lost state but sub-second detection switches within five seconds and costs one reconnection; and two exits with both gives recovery within five seconds that most sessions do not notice. A footer explains how to write the three values into a sentence the business can accept or reject.
svg.text: Availability is a product, not a sum: exits x state x detection
Two exits with no state coordination and a slow timer is not two nines better than one exit. It is one exit with a longer outage.
FACTOR 1
出口数（真分离）
两条链路 / 两台设备 / 两个池
共享层不分离 → 仍然计 1
x
FACTOR 2
状态能否同步
NAT 映射 / FW 会话 / VPN SA
取值：同步 / 重建 / 丢失
丢失 → 会话在切换时全断
x
FACTOR 3
检测速度
BFD / IP SLA / BGP / 人
取值：亚秒 / 秒 / 分钟
链路 up 路径坏 → 检测不到
FOUR COMBINATIONS, FOUR DIFFERENT OUTAGES
组合
用户实际体验
2 出口 · 状态丢失 · 分钟级检测
路由切了，会话全断，40 分钟报障
2 出口 · 状态同步 · 分钟级检测
会话能活，但流量仍走坏路径 180 s
2 出口 · 状态丢失 · 亚秒检测
5 s 内切换，用户需重连一次
2 出口 · 状态同步 · 亚秒检测
5 s 内恢复，多数会话无感
How to use the formula in a review
Write the three values down explicitly (exits 2, state = rebuilt not synchronised, detection = BFD 900 ms). Multiply them into a single
sentence about user experience, then ask whether that sentence is acceptable to the business owner. Nobody can argue with a sentence
the business understands: “a failure costs one reconnect within five seconds”.
The most expensive mistake in the table is row two: everything looks redundant, both links are up, and users still report an outage.
